title: raw SQL bulk updates and Dapper comparison
concepts: Raw SQL is useful when the query shape or database feature is not expressible in LINQ, but parameters must remain separate from SQL syntax. Interpolated and raw-string APIs have different safety contracts.
Entity-returning raw SQL participates in EF tracking according to the query mode and must return the expected mapped columns. Scalar SQL APIs have their own composability constraints.

ExecuteUpdate and ExecuteDelete issue set-based statements without loading entities or using the change tracker. They do not automatically apply tracked concurrency resolution or combine multiple calls into one transaction.

Dapper maps SQL results with little ORM behavior, while EF Core provides model mapping, LINQ translation, change tracking, and migrations. The choice depends on query control, mapping complexity, consistency, and team maintenance costs.
Using multiple data-access tools is possible, but transaction, connection, and mapping boundaries must remain explicit.

versionNotes.edition: EF Core 7 through 11 set-based DML; EF Core 11.0.0 stable
items: ExecuteUpdate and ExecuteDelete were introduced in EF Core 7 and remain the built-in set-based update/delete APIs in EF Core 11. EF Core 11.0.0 shipped on 2026-11-10 and requires .NET 11. These APIs are relational-provider dependent, execute immediately, and do not use or synchronize the change tracker; EF Core does not provide a matching built-in ExecuteInsert API in this scope. Bulk insertion and richer bulk semantics may require provider or third-party libraries.
